rationale: One major finding: the ResizableSeparator is always rendered regardless of panel state. When the config panel is collapsed (isConfigVisible=false), a user can drag the separator to expand the panel DOM-side, but ChatConfiguration's {isConfigVisible && ...} guard leaves the panel empty and the header toggle desynchronised. Fix: add an onOpen callback to useChatConfigResize and call it in handleResize when inPixels > 0 and isConfigVisible is false. All other raised concerns (pointer-global tracking, inPixels===0 equality, initial-mount race, viewport conflict) match patterns in the accepted useChatSidebarResize implementation and are deferred or dismissed. Commit format, types, and security are clean.

findings.problem: ResizableSeparator is always rendered regardless of panel collapsed state. When isConfigVisible=false and panel is at 0px, the 17px separator hit-area sits at the viewport's right edge. A user can drag it to expand the panel DOM-side. react-resizable-panels updates the DOM width, but ChatConfiguration guards its content with {isConfigVisible && ...}, so the panel grows but is empty. isConfigVisible stays false, so the Configuration header button also stays inactive.
findings.impact: User sees an expanding empty panel and the toggle button does not reflect the open state. No config controls are accessible. State and DOM are desynchronised.
findings.recommendation: Add onOpen: () => void to UseChatConfigResizeOptions. In handleResize, when panelSize.inPixels > 0 and !isConfigVisible (tracked via a ref or passed as a prop), call onOpen(). Wire it in ChatPage.tsx: onOpen: chatConfiguration.toggleConfigVisibility. Alternatively, conditionally render the separator only when isConfigVisible is true.
